paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company on a mission to revolutionize the current treatment paradigm for cystic fibrosis ("CF") by developing novel medicines that normalize the function of the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator ("CFTR") protein to deliver clinically meaningful benefit to people with CF. CF is a progressive and life-threatening genetic disease caused by inherited mutations in the CFTR gene, which lead to insufficient CFTR function. While advances in the discovery and development of CFTR modulators have significantly improved the lives of people with CF, at least two-thirds of patients on the current standard of care do not have normal CFTR function, defined as sweat chloride levels below 30 mmol/L. Patients with reduced CFTR function can experience debilitating multi-system complications that lead to significantly impaired quality of life and shorter life expectancy. Our goal is to deliver differentiated medicines for people with CF that can restore their CFTR function to as close to normal as possible by directly stabilizing CFTR's nucleotide binding domain 1 ("NBD1"). Despite having long been identified as a critical component for proper CFTR function, NBD1 has been considered "undruggable," and none of the currently approved CF therapies directly stabilizes NBD1. Leveraging more than a decade of our co-founders' research on NBD1, we are advancing a pipeline of small molecules engineered to correct the defects caused by the F508del genetic mutation, the most common CFTR mutation, which occurs in the NBD1 domain. Approximately 90% of people with CF carry at least one copy of the F508del genetic mutation.

We believe stabilizing NBD1 is central to unlocking dramatic improvements in clinical outcomes and quality of life for people with CF. The NBD1 domain of the CFTR protein, as illustrated in Figure 1 below, plays a key role in the folding, assembly, stability and trafficking of CFTR to a cell's surface, where it normally functions as an ion channel to regulate chloride and water transport. Within the NBD1 domain, F508del severely destabilizes CFTR, disrupting its proper assembly, impairing half-life and decreasing chloride channel function. We have employed biophysical, cell-based and virtual screening campaigns and extensive use of structural biology to guide the optimization of our novel small molecule NBD1 stabilizers. We are also advancing a portfolio of complementary CFTR modulator candidates designed to work synergistically with our NBD1 stabilizers to improve CFTR function, as seen in preclinical models.

We believe our robust pipeline provides multiple potential pathways to achieve our mission, either through development of an NBD1 stabilizer and a complementary modulator in combination with each other to produce a proprietary dual combination, or an NBD1 stabilizer administered in combination with the standard of care for CF. While we have prioritized development of a proprietary dual combination, we believe both development pathways offer attractive commercial opportunities.

Our proprietary portfolio is anchored by our NBD1 stabilizers and our complementary modulators. Our portfolio includes:

•SION-719, which is being evaluated as an add-on to the standard of care: SION-719, a highly potent NBD1 stabilizer, is currently in a Phase 2a proof-of-concept trial in CF patients, called PreciSION CF. The trial is evaluating SION-719 when administered with the standard of care for CF, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Inc.'s ("Vertex") Trikafta. Topline data from this trial is anticipated in mid-2026. In June 2025, we announced positive topline data from a Phase 1 trial of SION-719, which evaluated its pharmacokinetic ("PK") profile, safety and tolerability in healthy volunteers.

•SION-451, which is being evaluated in combinations with SION-2222 and SION-109: SION-451, a highly potent NBD1 stabilizer, is currently being evaluated in dual combinations with each of galicaftor (SION-2222) and SION-109, two of our complementary modulators, in a Phase 1 trial in healthy

volunteers. Topline data from this trial is anticipated in mid-2026. In June 2025, we announced positive topline data from the single agent portion of the Phase 1 trial, which evaluated SION-451's PK profile, safety and tolerability in healthy volunteers.

•SION-2222, a corrector that targets CFTR's transmembrane domain 1 ("TMD 1"), was generally well tolerated in Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials previously conducted by AbbVie Global Enterprises Ltd. ("AbbVie"). Improvement in sweat chloride as a monotherapy and improvements in sweat chloride and lung function as a combination therapy with navocaftor (SION-3067), a potentiator, were observed.
•SION-109, a corrector that targets CFTR's intracellular loop 4 ("ICL4") region, has been evaluated in a Phase 1 clinical trial in healthy volunteers, which was completed in 2024.

•Additional complementary modulators: We have additional CFTR modulators in our portfolio. SION-2851, a TMD1-directed CFTR corrector, has completed a Phase 1 single-ascending dose ("SAD") trial in healthy volunteers. SION-3067, a potentiator, has been evaluated in Phase 2 trials, where it demonstrated potential as a combination therapy.

We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company on a mission to revolutionize the current treatment paradigm for cystic fibrosis ("CF") by developing novel medicines that normalize the function of the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator ("CFTR") protein to deliver clinically meaningful benefit to people with CF. Our goal is to deliver differentiated medicines for people with CF that can restore their CFTR function to as close to normal as possible by directly stabilizing CFTR's nucleotide binding domain 1 ("NBD1"). We believe stabilizing NBD1 is central to unlocking dramatic improvements in clinical outcomes and quality of life for people with CF. We are also advancing a portfolio of complementary CFTR modulator candidates designed to work synergistically with our NBD1 stabilizers to improve CFTR function, as seen in preclinical models.

We believe our robust pipeline provides multiple potential pathways to achieve our mission, either through development of an NBD1 stabilizer and a complementary modulator in combination with each other to produce a proprietary dual combination, or an NBD1 stabilizer administered in combination with the standard of care for CF. While we have prioritized development of a proprietary dual combination, we believe both development pathways offer attractive commercial opportunities.

In June 2025, we announced positive topline data from our two randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled Phase 1 clinical trials evaluating SION-719 and SION-451, our lead NBD1 stabilizer product candidates, in healthy volunteers, and our plans to advance both compounds to the next phase of clinical development. The trials assessed the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics ("PK") of single and multiple ascending doses of each product candidate, as well as food effect and tablet bioequivalence.

Both SION-719 and SION-451 were generally well tolerated in these trials, with no serious adverse events, treatment emergent adverse events that led to discontinuation of drug, or dose-limiting toxicities observed. The Phase 1 data also supported the use of a tablet formulation in future trials and indicated that both compounds could be dosed in a fed or fasted state. Both NBD1 stabilizers met target exposure thresholds. Based on the Phase 1 data and our preclinical CF human bronchial epithelial ("CFHBE") model, we believe our NBD1 stabilizers have the potential to provide clinically meaningful benefit to people with CF when SION-719 is administered as an add-on to the standard of care or when SION-451 is used in proprietary dual combinations with one of our complementary modulators.
In October 2025, we announced the initiation of a Phase 2a proof-of-concept trial in CF patients evaluating SION-719 as an add-on to the standard of care. The Phase 2a trial, called PreciSION CF, is

designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and PK of SION-719 when administered with the standard of care for CF, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Inc.'s Trikafta, and to assess change in CFTR function as measured by sweat chloride levels. Additionally, in August 2025, we announced the initiation of a Phase 1 dual combination trial in healthy volunteers evaluating SION-451 in dual combinations with each of SION-2222 and SION-109, two of our complementary CFTR modulators. The trial will evaluate the safety, tolerability, and PK of varying doses of the dual combinations and will inform selection of a dual combination for further development. Topline data from both trials are anticipated in mid-2026.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段生技藥品公司，致力於革新現有囊腫性纖維化（"CF"）治療模式，透過開發創新藥物，使囊腫性纖維化跨膜導電調節器（"CFTR"）蛋白的功能正常化，以提供對CF患者的臨牀意義重大的療效。CF是一種進行性且危及生命的遺傳性疾病，由CFTR基因的遺傳突變所引起，導致CFTR功能不足。雖然CFTR調節劑的發現與開發進展已顯著改善CF患者的生存品質，但目前標準照護下至少有三分之二的患者CFTR功能不正常，定義為汗水氯離子濃度低於30 mmol/L。CFTR功能降低的患者可能會出現導致嚴重多系統併發症，進而造成顯著的生存品質下降與較短的預期壽命。本公司目標是為CF患者提供差異化的藥物，使其CFTR功能恢復至接近正常，透過直接穩定CFTR的核苷酸結合域1（"NBD1"）。儘管NBD1長久以來被認為是CFTR功能正常的重要組成部分，但NBD1一直被視為"無法藥物作用"，目前核准的CF治療藥物中，沒有直接穩定NBD1的藥物。透過我們共同創辦人超過十年對NBD1的研究，我們正在推動一系列小分子藥物，用以修正由F508del遺傳突變所造成的缺陷，這是CFTR最常見的突變，發生在NBD1區域。約有90%的CF患者至少攜帶一個F508del遺傳突變的拷貝。

本公司認為穩定NBD1是解鎖CF患者臨牀結果與生存品質顯著改善的關鍵。CFTR蛋白的NBD1區域，如圖1所示，對CFTR的摺疊、組裝、穩定性與向細胞表面的運輸發揮關鍵作用，CFTR在細胞表面通常作為離子通道，調節氯離子與水的運輸。在NBD1區域中，F508del嚴重降低CFTR的穩定性，幹擾其正確組裝，降低半衰期並減少氯離子通道功能。我們已運用生物物理、細胞基質及虛擬篩選活動，並廣泛使用結構生物學，以指導我們新型小分子NBD1穩定劑的優化。我們同時也在推動一系列補充性的CFTR調節劑候選藥物，設計為與我們的NBD1穩定劑協同作用，以改善CFTR功能，如預臨牀模型所顯示。
本公司認為我們強而有力的藥物開發管道提供多種潛在途徑，以實現我們的使命，無論是透過開發NBD1穩定劑與補充性調節劑組合，以產生專屬的雙重組合，或NBD1穩定劑與CF標準照護組合使用。雖然我們已優先發展專屬的雙重組合，但我們認為這兩種開發途徑都具有吸引人的商業機會。

本公司自有專利組合以NBD1穩定劑及補充調節劑為核心。本公司組合包括：

•SION-719，正被評估作為標準照護方案的附加治療：SION-719為一種高強度NBD1穩定劑，目前正進行Phase 2a概念驗證試驗，用於囊性纖維化（CF）患者，稱為PreciSION CF。該試驗評估SION-719與標準照護方案Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Inc.（"Vertex"）的Trikafta共同使用時的效果。此試驗的初步數據預計於2026年中公佈。2025年6月，本公司宣佈在SION-719的Phase 1試驗中獲得正面的初步數據，該試驗評估SION-719在健康志願者中的藥動學（"PK"）特性、安全性與耐受性。

•SION-451，正與SION-2222及SION-109組合評估：SION-451為一種高強度NBD1穩定劑，目前正於健康志願者中進行Phase 1試驗，評估其與galicaftor（SION-2222）及SION-109（本公司兩種補充調節劑）雙重組合的使用。此試驗的初步數據預計於2026年中公佈。2025年6月，本公司宣佈在Phase 1試驗的單一藥物部分獲得正面的初步數據，該試驗評估SION-451在健康志願者中的藥動學（"PK"）特性、安全性與耐受性。

•SION-2222，一種針對CFTR跨膜域1（"TMD 1"）的修正劑，於AbbVie Global Enterprises Ltd.（"AbbVie"）先前進行的第1期與第2期臨牀試驗中，通常被認為耐受性良好。單獨使用時觀察到汗水氯化物改善，與navocaftor（SION-3067）一種增效劑組合治療時，觀察到汗水氯化物與肺功能改善。

我們是一家臨牀階段生技藥品公司，目標是革新目前囊腫性纖維化（"CF"）之治療模式，透過開發創新藥物，使囊腫性纖維化跨膜導電調節器（"CFTR"）蛋白功能正常化，以提供對CF患者具有臨牀意義的治療效益。我們的目標是為CF患者提供差異化的藥物，使其CFTR功能恢復至接近正常狀態，透過直接穩定CFTR之核苷酸結合域1（"NBD1"）。我們認為穩定NBD1是解開對CF患者臨牀結果與生活品質產生顯著改善的關鍵。我們同時也在推進一組補充性的CFTR調節劑候選藥物，設計為與我們的NBD1穩定劑協同作用，以改善CFTR功能，如預臨牀模型所顯示的。
我們相信我們強大的藥物開發管道提供多種潛在途徑來實現我們的使命，或是透過開發NBD1穩定劑與補充性調節劑組合，以產生專屬的雙重組合，或是透過NBD1穩定劑與CF標準治療組合使用。雖然我們已優先發展專屬的雙重組合，我們認為這兩種開發途徑都具有吸引人的商業機會。
2025年6月，我們宣佈在健康志願者身上進行的兩項隨機雙盲安慰劑對照第一期臨牀試驗的初步數據為正面，評估我們的領先NBD1穩定劑候選藥物SION-719與SION-451，並宣佈計畫將兩種化合物推進至臨牀開發的下一階段。這些試驗評估了單次與多次遞增劑量下每種候選藥物的安全性、耐受性與藥動學（"PK"），以及食物影響與片劑生物等效性。

SION-719與SION-451在這些試驗中通常耐受良好，未觀察到嚴重不良事件、導致停藥的治療相關不良事件或劑量限制性毒性。第一期試驗數據也支持未來試驗中使用片劑製劑，並顯示兩種化合物可在進食或禁食狀態下給藥。兩種NBD1穩定劑均達到目標暴露門檻。根據第一期試驗數據與我們預臨牀CF人氣管上皮（"CFHBE"）模型，我們相信我們的NBD1穩定劑在SION-719作為標準治療的附加治療時，或是在SION-451與我們的補充性調節劑組合使用時，有潛力為CF患者提供臨牀意義的治療效益。
2025年10月，我們宣佈在CF患者中啟動一項第二期a期中證實概念試驗，評估SION-719作為標準治療的附加治療。此第二期a期試驗，稱為PreciSION CF，

設計用以評估SION-719在與CF標準治療、Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 的Trikafta共同使用時的安全性、耐受性與藥動學（"PK"），並評估CFTR功能的變化，以汗水氯離子水平衡量。此外，在2025年8月，我們宣佈在健康志願者中啟動一項第一期雙重組合試驗，評估SION-451與我們的補充性CFTR調節劑SION-2222與SION-109的雙重組合。該試驗將評估不同劑量下雙重組合的安全性、耐受性與藥動學（"PK"），並用以選擇進一步開發的雙重組合。兩項試驗的初步數據預計於2026年中公佈。

自本公司成立以來，我們主要透過私募 convertible preferred stock 之資金及 IPO 網路資金支應營運。2025 年，本公司完成 IPO，並透過銷售 12,176,467 股普通股，取得總計 199.6 百萬美元之淨資金，其中包括 1,588,234 股普通股係根據 underwriters 之選擇權購入額外股份所發行。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司已取得總計 530.0 百萬美元之淨資金。本公司尚未自產品銷售或其他來源產生任何營業收入。
由於我們投入大量研究、開發與製造費用，自成立以來已累積重大虧損與負現金流，包括截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日止年度分別為淨虧損256.4 百萬美元及75.3 百萬美元、61.7 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累積虧損為256.4 百萬美元。
我們預期費用及營運虧損將大幅增加，因我們：
•持續推進現有及未來產品候選藥物的臨牀開發；
•持續推進研究活動並尋求發現及開發更多產品候選藥物以擴充產品管線；
•追求任何成功完成臨牀試驗的現有或未來產品候選藥物的監管核准；
•持續委託第三方製造產品候選藥物；

本公司為一家臨牀階段生技製藥公司，擁有有限的營運歷史。自本公司成立以來，每年均產生營運虧損。本公司淨虧損為 75.3 百萬美元及 61.7 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日所結算年度的數字。本公司累計虧損為 256.4 百萬美元及 181.1 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日的數字。本公司營運虧損幾乎全部來自於研發計畫所產生的費用，以及與營運相關的總務及行政費用。本公司過去的虧損，加上預期未來的虧損，已對股東權益及營運資金造成負面影響，並會持續造成影響。

自 2019 年成立以來，本公司已將幾乎所有努力與財務資源投入產品候選品的開發、持續進行中的臨牀試驗、啟動新臨牀試驗以及持續製造以支持產品候選品。生技製藥產品的開發是一項高度風險且具高度不確定性的活動。本公司尚未證明具備進行後期臨牀試驗、取得監管核准、大規模製造任何產品或進行銷售與行銷活動以實現產品商業化的能耐，且無法保證未來會達成這些能力。本公司有限的營運歷史使得對本公司未來成功與生存能力的評估面臨重大不確定性。此外，若本公司取得任何產品候選品的行銷核准，將會產生重大銷售、行銷與製造費用。本公司預期會持續產生與作為上市公司營運相關的費用。因此，本公司預期會持續產生重大費用與營運虧損，且在可預見的未來會持續增加。由於開發藥物產品所涉及的眾多風險與不確定性，本公司無法預測未來虧損的程度，
以及何時會實現獲利，若能實現的話。即使本公司實現獲利，也可能無法維持或提高季度或年度的獲利能力。
